newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Israel's Frenkel says rate is to consolidate gains.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Frenkel says rate is to consolidate gains.

text.p: Jacob Frenkel, governor of the Bank of Israel, said the reason for holding the key lending rate for June stable at an annualised 13.9 percent was to consolidate the gains made in reducing inflation.

Frenkel also told Reuters Financial Television that the monetary policy of the Israeli central bank was very transparent and clear and anyone that wanted to make guesses about future interest rates should merely look at the country's inflation rate and make an assesment.

"If we are going to see inflation above target, we will not be able to loosen monetary policy. On the other hand if we see that inflation is falling at a rate faster than what the target is, then we will be able to modify our monetary policy," he said at the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
Frenkel noted that Israeli inflation had declined three percentage points since last summer and the government's target was to keep inflation between seven and 10 percent in 1997.
"We have made significant progress and we are now within target," he said, when asked about the background for holding rates steady on May 26.
"But it was very important the...inflation rate in Israel in the first four months was about 10 percent."
